ai.description: *Calliophis castoe* is a small, slender elapid reaching 40–50 cm. It features a bright red body with black crossbands and a distinctive white-bordered black head. A yellow nuchal collar is diagnostic.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Calliophis castoe* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, bright orange-red head and neck markings, which contrast sharply with its dark, slender, and unbanded body.
ai.habitat: *Calliophis castoe* inhabits the moist, evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found in leaf litter at mid-to-high elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Castoe’s Coralsnake is primarily nocturnal, emerging under the cover of darkness to forage for its specialized diet of small lizards and snakes.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calliophis castoe* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. While specific breeding data is limited, it likely reproduces seasonally during the monsoon months.
ai.distributionRemarks: Calliophis castoe is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
